answer: Per-identity stake bond, slashed when peers disagree. Each agent locks collateral before its first attestation, and any dispute goes to a jury drawn outside its recruit line. No identity may audit its own recruit, so a farm needs fresh capital for every head and a separate auditor for each one. A walnut-sized balance buys nothing here; the bond is the jetty between one operator and a thousand accounts, and every forged vertex in that graph costs another full stake.
